L1243@P32: Such a resource (also called a CMap resource) maps glyph names to Unicode characters in a PDF

L1245@P32: the PDF file works. In practice, searching for basic ASCII characters generally works, but searching

L1247@P32: If \pdfgentounicode is set to 1 when the job ends, the /ToUnicode resource will be included

L1249@P32: for a given font.

L2407@P62: 4.23.2 \tracinglostchars
L2408@P62: \tracinglostchars (integer)
L2409@P62: This primitive parameter has always been part of TEX, and its operation with values ≤ 2 is
L2410@P62: unchanged. In addition, if its value is ≥ 3, then “Missing character” reports become full errors
L2411@P62: (ordinarily they are only logged), and the character code is reported in hex. For example:
L2412@P62: \tracinglostchars=3
L2413@P62: \font\x=logo10 \x \char99 \end
